ESV.1: Then he led me out into the outer court, toward the north, and he brought me to the chambers that were opposite the separate yard and opposite the building on the north.
ESV.2: The length of the building whose door faced north was a hundred cubits,  and the breadth fifty cubits.
ESV.3: Facing the twenty cubits that belonged to the inner court, and facing the pavement that belonged to the outer court, was gallery  against gallery in three stories.
ESV.4: And before the chambers was a passage inward, ten cubits wide and a hundred cubits long,  and their doors were on the north.
ESV.5: Now the upper chambers were narrower, for the galleries took more away from them than from the lower and middle chambers of the building.
ESV.6: For they were in three stories, and they had no pillars like the pillars of the courts. Thus the upper chambers were set back from the ground more than the lower and the middle ones.
ESV.7: And there was a wall outside parallel to the chambers, toward the outer court, opposite the chambers, fifty cubits long.
ESV.8: For the chambers on the outer court were fifty cubits long, while those opposite the nave  were a hundred cubits long.
ESV.9: Below these chambers was an entrance on the east side, as one enters them from the outer court.
ESV.10: In the thickness of the wall of the court, on the south  also, opposite the yard and opposite the building, there were chambers
ESV.11: with a passage in front of them. They were similar to the chambers on the north, of the same length and breadth, with the same exits  and arrangements and doors,
ESV.12: as were the entrances of the chambers on the south. There was an entrance at the beginning of the passage, the passage before the corresponding wall on the east as one enters them.
ESV.13: Then he said to me, “The north chambers and the south chambers opposite the yard are the holy chambers, where the priests who approach the LORD shall eat the most holy offerings. There they shall put the most holy offerings — the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering — for the place is holy.
ESV.14: When the priests enter the Holy Place, they shall not go out of it into the outer court without laying there the garments in which they minister, for these are holy. They shall put on other garments before they go near to that which is for the people.”
ESV.15: Now when he had finished measuring the interior of the temple area, he led me out by the gate that faced east, and measured the temple area all around.
ESV.16: He measured the east side with the measuring reed, 500 cubits by the measuring reed all around.
ESV.17: He measured the north side, 500 cubits by the measuring reed all around.
ESV.18: He measured the south side, 500 cubits by the measuring reed.
ESV.19: Then he turned to the west side and measured, 500 cubits by the measuring reed.
ESV.20: He measured it on the four sides. It had a wall around it, 500 cubits long and 500 cubits broad, to make a separation between the holy and the common.

NLT.1: Then the man led me out of the Temple courtyard by way of the north gateway. We entered the outer courtyard and came to a group of rooms against the north wall of the inner courtyard.
NLT.2: This structure, whose entrance opened toward the north, was 175 feet long and 87 1⁄2 feet wide.
NLT.3: One block of rooms overlooked the 35-foot width of the inner courtyard. Another block of rooms looked out onto the pavement of the outer courtyard. The two blocks were built three levels high and stood across from each other.
NLT.4: Between the two blocks of rooms ran a walkway 17 1⁄2 feet wide. It extended the entire 175 feet of the complex, and all the doors faced north.
NLT.5: Each of the two upper levels of rooms was narrower than the one beneath it because the upper levels had to allow space for walkways in front of them.
NLT.6: Since there were three levels and they did not have supporting columns as in the courtyards, each of the upper levels was set back from the level beneath it.
NLT.7: There was an outer wall that separated the rooms from the outer courtyard; it was 87 1⁄2 feet long.
NLT.8: This wall added length to the outer block of rooms, which extended for only 87 1⁄2 feet, while the inner block — the rooms toward the Temple — extended for 175 feet.
NLT.9: There was an eastern entrance from the outer courtyard to these rooms.
NLT.10: On the south side of the Temple there were two blocks of rooms just south of the inner courtyard between the Temple and the outer courtyard. These rooms were arranged just like the rooms on the north.
NLT.11: There was a walkway between the two blocks of rooms just like the complex on the north side of the Temple. This complex of rooms was the same length and width as the other one, and it had the same entrances and doors. The dimensions of each were identical.
NLT.12: So there was an entrance in the wall facing the doors of the inner block of rooms, and another on the east at the end of the interior walkway.
NLT.13: Then the man told me, “These rooms that overlook the Temple from the north and south are holy. Here the priests who offer sacrifices to the LORD will eat the most holy offerings. And because these rooms are holy, they will be used to store the sacred offerings — the grain offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings.
NLT.14: When the priests leave the sanctuary, they must not go directly to the outer courtyard. They must first take off the clothes they wore while ministering, because these clothes are holy. They must put on other clothes before entering the parts of the building complex open to the public.”
NLT.15: When the man had finished measuring the inside of the Temple area, he led me out through the east gateway to measure the entire perimeter.
NLT.16: He measured the east side with his measuring rod, and it was 875 feet long.
NLT.17: Then he measured the north side, and it was also 875 feet.
NLT.18: The south side was also 875 feet,
NLT.19: and the west side was also 875 feet.
NLT.20: So the area was 875 feet on each side with a wall all around it to separate what was holy from what was common.

AMP.15: Now when he had finished measuring the inner temple, he brought me out toward the gate which faced east and measured the outer area all around.
AMP.16: He measured the east side with the measuring rod, five hundred rods by the measuring rod.
AMP.17: He measured the north side, five hundred rods by the measuring rod.
AMP.18: He measured the south side, five hundred rods by the measuring rod.
AMP.19: He turned about to the west side and measured five hundred rods by the measuring rod.
AMP.20: He measured it on the four sides; it had a wall all around, the length five hundred and the width five hundred, to make a separation between that which was holy [the temple proper] and that which was common [the outer area].

NIV.1:
Rooms for the Priests
Then the man led me northward into the outer court and brought me to the rooms opposite the temple courtyard and opposite the outer wall on the north side.
NIV.2: The building whose door faced north was a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide.
NIV.3: Both in the section twenty cubits from the inner court and in the section opposite the pavement of the outer court, gallery faced gallery at the three levels.
NIV.4: In front of the rooms was an inner passageway ten cubits wide and a hundred cubits long. Their doors were on the north.
NIV.5: Now the upper rooms were narrower, for the galleries took more space from them than from the rooms on the lower and middle floors of the building.
NIV.6: The rooms on the third floor had no pillars, as the courts had; so they were smaller in floor space than those on the lower and middle floors.
NIV.7: There was an outer wall parallel to the rooms and the outer court; it extended in front of the rooms for fifty cubits.
NIV.8: While the row of rooms on the side next to the outer court was fifty cubits long, the row on the side nearest the sanctuary was a hundred cubits long.
NIV.9: The lower rooms had an entrance on the east side as one enters them from the outer court.
NIV.10: On the south side along the length of the wall of the outer court, adjoining the temple courtyard and opposite the outer wall, were rooms
NIV.11: with a passageway in front of them. These were like the rooms on the north; they had the same length and width, with similar exits and dimensions. Similar to the doorways on the north
NIV.12: were the doorways of the rooms on the south. There was a doorway at the beginning of the passageway that was parallel to the corresponding wall extending eastward, by which one enters the rooms.
NIV.13: Then he said to me, “The north and south rooms facing the temple courtyard are the priests’ rooms, where the priests who approach the Lord will eat the most holy offerings. There they will put the most holy offerings—the grain offerings, the sin offerings and the guilt offerings—for the place is holy.
NIV.14: Once the priests enter the holy precincts, they are not to go into the outer court until they leave behind the garments in which they minister, for these are holy. They are to put on other clothes before they go near the places that are for the people.”
NIV.15: When he had finished measuring what was inside the temple area, he led me out by the east gate and measured the area all around:
NIV.16: He measured the east side with the measuring rod; it was five hundred cubits.
NIV.17: He measured the north side; it was five hundred cubits by the measuring rod.
NIV.18: He measured the south side; it was five hundred cubits by the measuring rod.
NIV.19: Then he turned to the west side and measured; it was five hundred cubits by the measuring rod.
NIV.20: So he measured the area on all four sides. It had a wall around it, five hundred cubits long and five hundred cubits wide, to separate the holy from the common.
